spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The decisive move is to replace a pointwise truncated zeta approximation by a smooth convolution. The truncation's explicit pole term grows troublesome below the square-root time scale, whereas smoothing turns the pole into a separately controllable residue and leaves a Fourier-filtered Dirichlet series for resonance.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Theorem 1 asserts unconditionally that for fixed 0 <= beta < 1 and positive c below sqrt(1-beta), sufficiently large T contains t in [T^beta,T] with an exponential lower bound for |zeta(1/2+it)|. The stated improvement in the leading constant is attributed to convolving zeta with a suitable smooth kernel instead of using the classical truncation whose pole term obstructs beta < 1/2.
directed.conceptual_reading: Smoothing changes the representation of the target without discarding the coefficient structure needed by the resonator: the global analytic obstruction is isolated as a residue rather than mixed into the main approximation. This exposes a proof-design principle in which the transform is chosen to make a singular contribution harmless over the desired localization range.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: A Cauchy-kernel formula transfers large log-zeta values into lower bounds for the primitive S1
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Starting from a conditional integral representation of log absolute zeta in terms of S, integration by parts replaces S with S1 and an explicit signed kernel. Choosing sigma just to the right of the critical line then imports an earlier large-value result to obtain a preliminary conditional S1 bound.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Contour shifting turns a smoothed zeta value into a weighted Dirichlet series plus an explicit pole residue
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Lemma 1 shifts a contour from the critical strip to an absolutely convergent line, expands zeta there, and shifts each kernel integral back. The result cleanly separates Fourier-selected Dirichlet coefficients from the residue of the zeta pole.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Using larger primes and a longer resonator increases the detectable Dirichlet-series amplitude, but weakens localization and currently loses control of how often the extremes occur. More fundamentally, nonnegative resonator coefficients make the method a positive-real-part selector, so they do not recover both signs the way high moments can.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source contrasts its resonance method with Selberg-Tsang high moments and with an earlier shorter resonator. Larger primes and a longer Dirichlet polynomial improve maxima but require substantially larger intervals and have not produced a reasonable measure estimate for the large-value set. It states that nonnegative coefficients allow the resonator to catch large positive real parts, obstructing improved conditional Omega-plus/minus results for S and an improved Omega-minus result for S1.
directed.conceptual_reading: The resonator architecture fixes both sensitivity and blind spots: support length controls amplitude versus localization, while coefficient positivity supplies monotonicity at the cost of sign symmetry. These are structural tradeoffs, not merely loose constants.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Resonance bridges a Dirichlet series to a weighted mean dominated by chosen multiplicative correlations; high moments provide the comparison bridge that can detect either sign and support measure estimates.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The claimed adaptability of an earlier measure result and Tsang's proof is mentioned without proof. No stronger measure theorem is supplied, so an unconditional version of the later S1 result remains a hope. Positivity explicitly blocks the missing sign results.
directed.uncertainty: The methodological claims and stated obstruction are clear in the text; quantitative comparisons with the cited works cannot be independently assessed from this span.
